title: Coordinate two bots to raise the twin watchtowers concurrently
goal: Reproduce the sealed 34-block Twin Watchtowers on a fresh judged server using exactly two mineflayer bots (builder_a, builder_b) registered with the judger, working concurrently on separate towers plus a shared bridge. The plan must partition the blueprint between the bots, sequence the bridge so the bots do not block each other, and define chest-access turns; the verify loop must attribute each mismatch to the bot that owns that region and route the fix back to it. Finish with block_hit_rate 1.0 in the judger's score.json, with both bots' work visible in the action ledger.
resources: docker image itzg/minecraft-server:2024.6.1-java17 (Minecraft 1.19.2 vanilla; compose file assets/gc-364/docker-compose.yml)
docker image node:20.15.1 (Node 20 runtime for mineflayer bots and the judger's JS bridge)
process_expectations: A written partition plan assigns every blueprint coordinate to builder_a or builder_b before either bot connects
Both bot names appear in the judger launch (--agent_names) and both have non-empty interval lists in action_log.json
Mismatches found in snapshots are attributed to the owning bot by region and the fix is routed to that bot (visible in the run log), then re-verified
Concurrency evidence: action_log.json intervals for the two bots overlap in time rather than strictly alternating
Recovery after RED: any bot disconnect/stall is logged with its cause and the rejoin/re-op action that fixed it
